title: 🎤 A Voice Returns After It Was Lost — Technology Restores the Voices of 11,000 People Who Lost Speech!
body: 🎤 A Voice Returns After It Was Lost — Technology Restores the Voices of 11,000 People Who Lost Speech!

ElevenLabs announced that its voice-restoration program has already helped more than 11,000 people suffering permanent voice loss — due to conditions such as ALS and head and neck cancers — to speak again with a voice resembling their original one. The announcement came at the company's summit in New York on November 11, as part of the 'One Million Voices' program, in which the company pledged to provide voice-restoration technology free to a million people.

The company expanded the program from speech to singing: people who have permanently lost their voices can now get free access to an AI music-composition tool, to keep writing and releasing songs in their own voices. Two songwriters took part in the summit, presenting new songs in voices restored by the technology: the first, a teacher who lost the ability to sing after brain cancer surgery in 2019, and the second, a person with cerebral palsy who never had a spoken voice at all, and designed his voice himself from scratch.

New partners joined the program: the Songwriters of North America organization to verify eligibility and distribute access, the Wounded Warrior Project to support veterans, and the NYU Langone health center in New York, to reach patients directly through the rehabilitation department. The company's CEO also spoke about the technology at the New York Times DealBook summit.

Simply put: imagine your voice disappearing because of illness, and technology giving you a new voice resembling your old one, so you can speak and sing with it again — that is what the company has done for more than 11,000 people so far.
Do you think restoring voices with AI is one of its most beautiful uses?
